key_insight: Modeling the static environment as an implicit 3D representation allows decoupling scene context from dynamic subjects, enabling photorealistic, camera-consistent cinematic videos from a few environment images and a user-specified camera trajectory.
problem_solved: Generates high-quality cinematic video of moving subjects inside a fixed scene while preserving scene consistency and camera coherence, without building physical sets or extensive multi-view capture.
method: Fit an implicit 3D scene representation from multiple input images to capture geometry, appearance, and view-dependent effects.
Decouple and synthesize dynamic subject motion separately, then composite/render the subject into the implicit scene to maintain correct occlusion and lighting.
Render a temporally coherent video by following a user-specified camera trajectory through the implicit scene.
impact: Makes controllable, production-quality virtual cinematography accessible from limited scene captures, reducing cost and enabling new workflows in VFX, virtual production, and data generation for video models.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: inputs (scene images + camera path) → implicit 3D scene → subject module → renderer → output video frames
Side-by-side comparison: static input photos vs synthesized cinematic frames along a camera move
Occlusion and lighting inset: subject correctly occluded/illuminated by implicit scene geometry
Camera trajectory overlay on a 3D scene preview showing sampled frames along the path
paper_title: CineScene: Implicit 3D as Effective Scene Representation for Cinematic Video Generation
paper_authors: Kaiyi Huang, Yukun Huang, Yu Li, Jianhong Bai, Xintao Wang
